Where it began

Tim Southee was born in Whangārei on 11 December 1988 and grew up in Northland. At Whangārei Boys' High School and then King's College in Auckland he was good enough at rugby to play it at representative level, but cricket won.

He was a star of New Zealand's youth sides, alongside future team-mates such as Kane Williamson and Trent Boult. At the 2008 Under-19 World Cup in Malaysia he took 17 wickets in five games at 6.64 and was named player of the tournament. Within a month he was a Test cricketer.

The player

His Test debut, against England at Napier in March 2008, came at 19 years and 102 days. He took five wickets, removing Michael Vaughan, Andrew Strauss and Kevin Pietersen among them, and then, with the match long gone, smashed 77 not out from 40 balls with nine sixes.

He went on to play 107 Tests over 16 years, taking 391 wickets at 30.26 with 15 five-wicket innings and a best of 7 for 64 against India at Bangalore. Only 18 men in Test history have taken more wickets. He was part of the side that won the first World Test Championship, and from December 2022 to October 2024 he captained New Zealand in 14 Tests. One of them, against England in February 2023, was won by a single run after New Zealand had followed on.

What made him special

He moved the ball late and away from the bat, and as the years went by he added slower cutters that, on a damp pitch, behaved almost like brisk off-spin. He and Trent Boult shared the new ball for years, a partnership that served New Zealand well for a long time.

Nobody ever mistook him for a top-order batsman, and his average of 15.48 agrees. But few lower-order men have been more fun to watch. He made 7 Test fifties, and his 98 sixes came at a rate of one every 27 balls, a pace nobody else had matched when he retired.

Away from the middle

In one-day cricket he once took 7 for 33 against England at the 2015 World Cup, a spell Wisden later called the one-day spell of the decade. He was the first New Zealander to reach 700 international wickets, and he took two hat-tricks in Twenty20 internationals. He also played franchise cricket in India and county cricket for Essex. In the 2025 King's Birthday Honours he became an Officer of New Zealand's Order of Merit.

And finally

In August 2019 he drew level with Sachin Tendulkar for Test sixes, on 69. It is not a list most people expected a fast bowler to share with Tendulkar, and he did not stop there.
